description.narrative:
Smallholder coffee farmers in the Mt. Elgon region, within Bushika Area Cooperative Enterprise (BIACE), continue to face intertwined challenges that undermine productivity and household resilience. Steep terrain, recurrent landslides, soil erosion, shifting rainfall patterns, and limited extension services have led to declining yields and persistent food insecurity. These constraints are compounded by poor agronomic practices, inadequate farm inputs, limited access to affordable finance, weak post-harvest management, and restricted participation of women and youth due to structural barriers such as limited land ownership and underrepresentation in leadership.
The proposed three-year project, Livelihoods for Smallholder Coffee Farmers, aims to strengthen BIACE into a competitive, climate-resilient cooperative capable of driving inclusive economic transformation. The initiative will enhance coffee quality and productivity, expand climate-smart and agro-ecological farming, and strengthen governance across the 16 primary societies representing 1,778 farmers. Focus areas include improving value addition, reducing post-harvest losses, advancing gender equality, and broadening market access through certification and collective marketing.
By investing in stronger cooperative systems, sustainable production, and equitable participation, the project seeks to secure stable incomes, improve food security, and build long-term resilience for coffee-dependent households on the Mt. Elgon slopes. Ultimately, it positions BIACE as a model agribusiness championing inclusive growth in Bududa District.
